node.name: battery_support_router
node.description: Decide what the battery system owner needs from the support desk.

conditions.a: The owner reports a fault, error code or abnormal behaviour of the battery system.
conditions.b: The owner asks how to change the battery's charging schedule or operating mode.
conditions.c: The customer asks about credits or payments for energy exported to the grid.
conditions.d: The owner wants to claim a warranty replacement for a battery unit already diagnosed faulty.
conditions.e: The owner wants to add another battery module to increase storage capacity.
conditions.f: The owner wants to update contact or ownership details on the account.

ctx: Hi, I have a question about my home battery.
Sure, what's going on with it?
examples.msg: The app shows a red triangle with E-214 and the battery has sat at 40% all day even though the panels are producing.
examples.why: error code and stuck charge describe a fault

ctx: Good morning, I hope you're keeping well.
Good morning! What can I help you with today?
examples.msg: Thank you so much. So, we had the unit installed two summers ago and it was lovely until your technician confirmed last week that one of the modules is dead, so there is nothing new for me to report as a fault. He said it's still within the warranty period, so I would simply like to claim a swap under that warranty, if that's how it works. My husband says hello, by the way.
examples.why: warranty claim for a known dead module, not a fault report

examples.msg: So I noticed my bill credit's been zero for three months even though the battery dumps power back to the grid every evening.
examples.why: missing export credit on bill

examples.msg: The battery keeps topping up from the grid at like 5pm when rates are highest, I'd rather it filled up overnight.
examples.why: wants charging to happen at another time

examples.msg: We've bought an electric car and the one battery box in the garage runs out by midnight. Can we get another box put in next to it so it holds more?
examples.why: wants extra unit for more storage

node.name: drone_registry_router
node.description: Decide which registry or licensing service the caller needs.

ctx: Good afternoon. I have a question regarding one of my registered drones.
Certainly. What would you like to do with it?
examples.msg: I have sold the aircraft to a colleague, and I would like the registration to be moved into her name so that she can continue to fly it legally.
examples.why: sold drone, registration moved to buyer: transfer, not offered

ctx: Hi, this is the drone registry assistant. What do you need today?
examples.msg: Hey, I think my pilot card fell out of my wallet at the park, need a new one sent over.
examples.why: lost licence card needs replacing

ctx: Hello, I am a licensed operator.
Welcome. How may I assist you?
examples.msg: This morning my drone lost signal and came down on a neighbour's greenhouse, breaking two panes. I understand I am required to notify the authority.
examples.why: crash with damage must be reported

ctx: Hello, how can I help you today?
examples.msg: Oh hello, thank you. I've been flying for years, mostly photographing the coastline near my cottage, but last month my old quadcopter went into the sea and it is well and truly gone. I'd like it taken off my record since it no longer exists. Also, your website was rather slow this morning, just so you know.
examples.why: destroyed drone removed from record; website is side note

ctx: Welcome to the drone registry. What can I do for you?
examples.msg: I not want to register new drone, I have it already. I need permission for fly near the harbour area for film the festival on Saturday.
examples.why: permission to fly in specific area

node.name: outreach_request_router
node.description: Decide what a school or member of the public wants from the agency outreach team.

conditions.a: The person asks to book a guided visit to the visitor centre or launch viewing area for a group, such as a school class or club.
conditions.b: The person asks for a scientist or astronaut to give a talk at their school or event, either in person or by video call.
conditions.c: The person wants free classroom materials, such as lesson plans, posters or activity kits, about space missions for teaching purposes.
conditions.d: The person asks about the current status or schedule of a specific mission, for example a launch date, a delay or a landing time.
conditions.e: The person asks how to apply for internships, student programmes or jobs at the agency, including eligibility and application deadlines.
conditions.f: The person wants to change or cancel a visit booking they have already made, for example moving it to a new date or reducing the number of visitors.
conditions.g: The person wants to use agency images or video footage in a publication, film or product and asks about permission, licensing or credit lines.

examples.msg: school yearbook cover. that mars rover photo off your site. ok to print it
examples.why: wants to reuse agency photo in print

ctx: Hello! I can see your booking: a guided visitor centre tour for 32 pupils from Ashwell Primary on 14 March. What can I help you with?
examples.msg: Oh, how lovely that you have it right there. Well, it's a bit of a story, the headteacher has scheduled the school inspection for that very week, of all weeks, so would it be at all possible to make it the 21st instead? The children would be heartbroken to miss out.
examples.why: moving the existing tour to another date

examples.msg: So we've got the whole family set to watch the lunar lander go up Thursday morning and now I'm hearing rumours about the weather. Is it still on?
examples.why: asks whether a launch is still scheduled

ctx: Hi, I'm a science teacher at a secondary school.
Hello! How can the outreach team help you?
examples.msg: Our Year 9s have a careers week in May and they'd love to hear first-hand from someone who actually works on the rover missions.
examples.why: wants an agency expert to speak to pupils

examples.msg: My daughter is studying physics at university and wants to, I don't know, work with you over the summer? Like a trial job for students? Is that even possible?
examples.why: student summer work means internship application

ctx: Hi, this is the space agency outreach team. How can we help?
examples.msg: My car's been making a grinding noise for a week and every garage is closed. What the hell is wrong with it?
examples.why: car repair unrelated to space outreach

node.name: scaff_ops_router
node.description: Route incoming scaffolding customer requests to the right ops queue.

conditions.a: New enq - quote for supply + erect
conditions.b: Hire ext - keep scaff up past off-hire date
conditions.c: Full strike - job done, dismantle + collect all kit
conditions.d: Adaption - add lifts, loading bay or hoist to live scaff
conditions.e: Insp/handover cert - request scaff tag or inspection report
conditions.f: Defect report - damaged or unsafe scaff on site
conditions.g: Erect delay - crew/delivery not turned up, chase ETA
conditions.h: Part strike - remove some lifts/bays, rest stays up
conditions.i: Acct query - invoice or hire charge dispute
conditions.j: Pavement licence - council permit for scaff on public footway

examples.msg: Hey, the roofers finished yesterday so you can come take the whole lot down whenever suits.
examples.why: work done, remove all scaffolding

examples.msg: Hello there, I hope your week is going well. The brickwork on the front elevation is finally finished, which we're thrilled about after all that rain, so if your lads could take down the scaffold on the front only, that would be marvellous; the back still needs to stay up for the roofers next month. Many thanks indeed.
examples.why: only front removed, back stays: partial strike, not offered

examples.msg: The council just stuck a notice on the scaffold saying there's no permit for it being on the pavement. Sort it out. And your driver blocked my drive again.
examples.why: missing footway permit; driver complaint is side issue

examples.msg: After storm last night, some boards on the top level is hanging down and one pole is bent. Workers is afraid to go up.
examples.why: storm damage makes scaffold unsafe

ctx: Thanks for contacting us. What can we help with?
examples.msg: Been stood on site since 7 with a gang of bricklayers doing nothing. Scaffold was meant to go up this morning. Nobody's here.
examples.why: erection crew has not arrived

ctx: Hi, it's about the job at 12 Mill Lane.
Thanks. The scaffold there is booked to come down on Friday the 6th. What would you like to do?
examples.msg: Can we push that back another three weeks? The plasterers are running late.
examples.why: postpone take-down means extending hire

node.name: lift_callout_slot_reply
node.description: Classify what kind of information the caller's reply gives to the assistant's question.

ctx: I need to book the annual service for our two passenger lifts.
Of course. Which day this month would suit you for the engineer to attend?
examples.msg: The 12th, if that's free.
examples.why: answers which day: a date

ctx: Thanks for calling the breakdown line. Which lift is it? There should be a number on the plate inside the car.
examples.msg: It's freaking number 4 mate, the one that's always knackered.
examples.why: number from the lift plate

ctx: Hi, the lift at our block is making a weird noise.
Sorry to hear that. Can you give me the address of the building?
examples.msg: Sorry, totally different thing, but do you know if chemists open on bank holidays? The late ones, whatever they're called?
examples.why: pharmacy hours unrelated to lifts

ctx: Hello, one of our lifts keeps stopping between floors.
I can log a call-out. Where is the building?
examples.msg: It's the big block, I think it's called Harwood Court? On Fenn Street, number 48 maybe.
examples.why: gives building name and street

ctx: I'd like to report a problem with a lift.
Thanks. Can you give me the lift ID from the plate in the car?
examples.msg: The doors keep opening and shutting on the ground floor and it just won't go anywhere.
examples.why: describes the malfunction instead of the ID

node.name: survey_job_router
node.description: Decide what the surveying client wants to do.

conditions.a: The client wants to dispute the result of a boundary survey already completed.
conditions.b: The client wants a topographic survey of a site for design work.
conditions.c: The client asks about the status or delivery date of their survey report.
conditions.d: The client wants construction stakeout marking building positions on site.
conditions.e: The client wants a quote for drone mapping of a large area.
conditions.f: The client wants to reschedule a booked field visit to another date.
conditions.g: The client asks about invoices or payment for survey work.
conditions.h: The client wants to book a boundary survey to establish property lines.

examples.msg: I need someone to work out exactly where my land ends and my neighbour's begins before we put up a new fence.
examples.why: wants property line established

ctx: Hello, how can we help with your project?
examples.msg: Our foundation crew starts on Monday and needs the corners of the new warehouse marked out on the ground. Also, your last invoice had the wrong PO number on it.
examples.why: marking building corners; invoice is side topic

ctx: Hey, you guys did a boundary survey on my place in June.
Thanks for getting in touch. What can we do for you?
examples.msg: So the line you drew puts my shed on next door's land and I'm pretty sure that's wrong. I want to challenge it.
examples.why: contests completed boundary result, not offered

ctx: topo survey done last week at 14 orchard rd
Thanks. What would you like to know about that job?
examples.msg: report. when. architect waiting
examples.why: asks when report arrives

examples.msg: Your guy is supposed to come and measure the field on Thursday but I'll be away. Can that thing be moved? Not sure what you call it, the site visit?
examples.why: move booked visit to another day

node.name: solar_project_slot_reply
node.description: Classify what kind of answer the customer gives to the assistant's question.

ctx: Your roof survey is ready to be booked. Which day would suit you for the surveyor to visit?
examples.msg: Oh, how exciting. Well, I work from home most of the week, though Mondays are my pottery class, which I'd hate to miss. So perhaps the Wednesday of the week after next would be ideal, if your surveyor is free then.
examples.why: names a specific day for visit

ctx: To prepare your grid connection application, please send your electricity meter serial number.
examples.msg: Before I do that, can you tell me how long the panel warranty lasts?
examples.why: asks warranty question instead of answering

ctx: I'd like to move forward with the installation.
Great. Would you prefer the 6.4 kW or the 8 kW system?
examples.msg: Could you email me the installation contract first so I can read through it?
examples.why: requests contract, no answer to choice

ctx: The surveyor said there are two layout options for my roof.
That's right: option one puts all 14 panels on the south side, option two splits them across east and west. Which would you like?
examples.msg: The split one, please.
examples.why: chooses option two

ctx: To set up your export application, could you tell me the rated capacity of your existing inverter?
examples.msg: Sorry, the previous owners put it in and left no paperwork at all, and I've honestly never even opened that cupboard. I hope that doesn't hold everything up?
examples.why: implies they cannot tell the capacity

node.name: licence_answer_followup
node.description: Classify how the customer reacts to the assistant's answer about image licensing.

conditions.a: Does the user indicate the answer resolved their question?
conditions.b: Does the user say the answer is wrong or does not match what they see?
conditions.c: Does the user want more detail about the same answer?

ctx: A standard licence lets you use the image on websites and in print up to 500,000 copies.
examples.msg: Other thing: where I can find the invoice for my order from last month?
examples.why: switches to invoice request; no condition covers

ctx: Editorial images can be used in commercial advertising once you buy the extended licence.
examples.msg: Funny, the licence page I read yesterday said editorial pictures can never go in ads, whatever you pay.
examples.why: hints the answer contradicts the policy

ctx: Can I use a photo I licensed on a book cover?
Yes, the standard licence covers book covers for print runs up to 500,000 copies.
examples.msg: Great, our first print run is only 3,000, so we're well inside that.
examples.why: confirms answer fits their case

ctx: Yes, cropping and colour adjustments are allowed under every licence type.
examples.msg: perfect. all set
examples.why: acknowledges answer, done

ctx: yo can i use your pics on merch
Yes, you need the extended licence for products for resale, such as t-shirts and mugs.
examples.msg: aight cool but like, how many freaking shirts can I crank out before I hit some cap or whatever?
examples.why: wants limits detail on extended licence

ctx: What resolution will I receive with the medium size option?
The medium size is delivered at 2000 by 1333 pixels.
examples.msg: That does not match the file in my downloads at all.
examples.why: says stated resolution differs from reality

node.name: restoration_handoff
node.description: Decide whether the client needs a conservator or can continue the automated drop-off booking.

conditions.a: Hand off to conservator for condition advice

examples.msg: The chair's wrapped and already in the car, I just need to know which slot is free on Friday.
examples.why: ready to drop off, needs slot

ctx: I can book a drop-off slot for your piece now, or put you through to one of our conservators. Which would you prefer?
examples.msg: The former. Condition report's already been done by our registrar.
examples.why: chooses booking the drop-off

ctx: Welcome to the workshop. How can I help today?
examples.msg: Our oil portrait has developed fine cracks across the varnish and some flaking near the frame, and I am unsure whether it is safe to transport.
examples.why: damage needs expert assessment

ctx: Thanks. What do you need help with?
examples.msg: invoice. never got it. need a copy
examples.why: billing request, neither conservator nor booking

examples.msg: Hey, do you guys ever buy old furniture outright? I've got a sideboard I'd sell.
examples.why: selling furniture not covered

node.name: consignment_router
node.description: Decide what the seller wants from the consignment department.

ctx: My clock is in the June sale, lot 112.
Thanks. Its reserve is currently set at 800. What would you like to do?
examples.msg: Can we drop it to 600?
examples.why: lowers the reserve amount

examples.msg: My late aunt's silver tea set has been sitting in a cupboard for years and nobody in the family wants it. Your spring sale looks like just the place for it.
examples.why: implies entering item into auction

examples.msg: bidder registration. how. next sale
examples.why: buyer registration not a seller option

ctx: Good morning. My painting was sold in your March sale.
Congratulations. Proceeds are paid 35 days after the sale, less commission. Is there anything else?
examples.msg: It has now been seven weeks and nothing has arrived in my account.
examples.why: proceeds overdue after sale

examples.msg: dude the sale with my old guitars was yesterday and I've been on edge all freaking night, did they go or what?
examples.why: wants to know if lots sold
